Pow(x,n).problem: Compute x raised to an int exponent using IEEE-754 double arithmetic; 0^0 returns 1.
Pow(x,n).approach: Binary exponentiation keeps ans*x^remaining equal to the desired result. Consume low bits; square the base as the exponent halves.
Pow(x,n).trace: 2^-3 becomes 0.5^3: take 0.5, square to 0.25, then take it -> 0.125.
Pow(x,n).pitfalls: Cast exponent to long before negating MIN_VALUE. Double overflow/underflow follows IEEE-754; this is not exact rational arithmetic.

Generate Parentheses.problem: Generate all balanced strings with n opening and n closing parentheses; n=0 yields one empty string.
Generate Parentheses.approach: Only add an opening when open<n, and a closing when close<open. These conditions ensure no invalid prefix is generated; every balanced string follows one such path.
Generate Parentheses.complexity: O(n*C_n) time/output space where C_n is the nth Catalan number; O(n) recursion/path space.
Generate Parentheses.trace: At n=2 paths are (()) and ()(); trying to close at the initial state is forbidden.
Generate Parentheses.pitfalls: Restore the builder after each branch. The returned list is exponential; large n cannot be enumerated practically.

Power Set.problem: Enumerate positional subsets; skip branch is visited before take branch. Duplicate values may give equal value lists.
Power Set.approach: At each index choose skip or take. Copy the path at a leaf to prevent later mutations from changing stored results.
Power Set.complexity: O(n*2^n) time/output space; O(n) stack and working path.
Power Set.pitfalls: Use remove(size-1), not remove(value), when restoring a path. Enumeration includes the empty subset.
Power Set.alternatives: Bitmask enumeration gives the same asymptotic costs with a different order.

Count Good Numbers.problem: Length-n digit strings have an even digit at every zero-based even position and a prime digit at every odd position. Leading zeros allowed; return modulo 1e9+7.
Count Good Numbers.approach: Even positions have five choices {0,2,4,6,8}; odd positions four {2,3,5,7}. Independent choices multiply, so use 5^ceil(n/2)*4^floor(n/2) with modular exponentiation.
Count Good Numbers.trace: n=4 has two positions of each kind: 5²*4²=400.
Count Good Numbers.pitfalls: Use n/2+n%2 rather than (n+1)/2 to avoid long overflow. n=0 represents one empty string.

Reverse a Stack.problem: Reverse a stack in place, using the front of ArrayDeque as its top.
Reverse a Stack.approach: Remove the top recursively; after reversing the remaining stack, insert the saved top at the bottom via a second recursion.
Reverse a Stack.complexity: O(n²) time; O(n) peak recursion space.
Reverse a Stack.trace: Pop 1,2,3; insert 3 at bottom of empty, then 2 below 3, then 1 below them.
Reverse a Stack.pitfalls: Deque iteration prints top-to-bottom here. Deep recursion can overflow the Java stack.
Reverse a Stack.alternatives: A second stack reverses in O(n) time with O(n) auxiliary storage.

Learn All Patterns of Subsequences (Theo.theory: At index i, a positional subsequence either includes a[i] or skips it. Recurse on i+1 in both cases; the measure n-i decreases. A mutable path needs push -> recurse -> pop restoration. At i==n: print/copy the path for enumeration, return whether its sum matches for existence, or return 1/0 for counting. Existence can short-circuit with OR; counting adds both branches. Duplicated values still give distinct positional choices. Pruning sum>target is only safe when all remaining values are nonnegative. Worst case is 2^n leaves and O(n) stack, with additional output cost when copying paths.

Check if there exists a subsequence with.problem: Decide if some positional subsequence sums to k; empty subsequence is allowed.
Check if there exists a subsequence with.approach: Take/skip every index. The leaf tests the remaining target. OR combines the branches and short-circuits on a witness.
Check if there exists a subsequence with.complexity: O(2^n) recursive nodes; O(n) stack. BigInteger counting cost additionally depends on count bits.
Check if there exists a subsequence with.trace: [1,2,1] reaches sum 2 either by taking index 1 alone or both indices 0,2.
Check if there exists a subsequence with.pitfalls: Negatives and zeros are supported, so sum-based positive-only pruning is intentionally absent.
Check if there exists a subsequence with.alternatives: Memoize (index,remaining) to avoid repeated states. Nonnegative bounded sums admit subset-sum DP; existence can use a boolean table, counting an integer table.

Count all subsequences with sum K.problem: Count positional subsequences summing to k, including the empty one for k=0.
Count all subsequences with sum K.approach: Take/skip every index. The leaf tests the remaining target. Counts add because the branches partition positional subsets.
Count all subsequences with sum K.complexity: O(2^n) recursive nodes; O(n) stack. BigInteger counting cost additionally depends on count bits.
Count all subsequences with sum K.trace: [1,2,1] reaches sum 2 either by taking index 1 alone or both indices 0,2.
Count all subsequences with sum K.pitfalls: Negatives and zeros are supported, so sum-based positive-only pruning is intentionally absent.
Count all subsequences with sum K.alternatives: Memoize (index,remaining) to avoid repeated states. Nonnegative bounded sums admit subset-sum DP; existence can use a boolean table, counting an integer table.

Generate Binary Strings Without Consecut.problem: Generate length-n binary strings in lexicographic order, forbidding adjacent ones.
Generate Binary Strings Without Consecut.approach: Zero is always allowed; one is allowed only after zero or at the first position. This excludes invalid prefixes immediately while preserving all valid choices.
Generate Binary Strings Without Consecut.trace: After prefix 01 only zero is allowed, producing 010.
Generate Binary Strings Without Consecut.pitfalls: n=0 gives the single empty string. Save the allowed-one condition before appending/removing zero.

Combination Sum.problem: Find unique nondecreasing combinations summing to target, with positive candidates. Each candidate may be reused.
Combination Sum.approach: Sort candidates, skip duplicate siblings, and append values only at/after start. Recurse at i for reuse. This makes combinations canonical and avoids permutation duplicates.
Combination Sum.complexity: Exponential output-sensitive time; O(target/minCandidate) recursion depth for reuse, O(n) without reuse, plus sorted copy/output.
Combination Sum.trace: For target 7, reusing 2 gives 2+2+3; candidate 7 gives a singleton. Without reuse only [7] is possible.
Combination Sum.pitfalls: Zero candidates would create infinite reuse recursion; reject nonpositive values. A remaining target of zero yields one completed combination.

Combination Sum II.problem: Find unique nondecreasing combinations summing to target, with positive candidates. Each input position may be used once.
Combination Sum II.approach: Sort candidates, skip duplicate siblings, and append values only at/after start. Recurse at i+1 to prevent reuse. This makes combinations canonical and avoids permutation duplicates.
Combination Sum II.complexity: Exponential output-sensitive time; O(target/minCandidate) recursion depth for reuse, O(n) without reuse, plus sorted copy/output.
Combination Sum II.trace: For target 7, reusing 2 gives 2+2+3; candidate 7 gives a singleton. Without reuse only [7] is possible.
Combination Sum II.pitfalls: Zero candidates would create infinite reuse recursion; reject nonpositive values. A remaining target of zero yields one completed combination.

Subsets I.problem: Enumerate positional subsets; skip branch is visited before take branch. Duplicate values may give equal value lists.
Subsets I.approach: At each index choose skip or take. Copy the path at a leaf to prevent later mutations from changing stored results.
Subsets I.complexity: O(n*2^n) time/output space; O(n) stack and working path.
Subsets I.pitfalls: Use remove(size-1), not remove(value), when restoring a path. Enumeration includes the empty subset.
Subsets I.alternatives: Bitmask enumeration gives the same asymptotic costs with a different order.

Subsets II.problem: Enumerate distinct value subsets when input can contain duplicates.
Subsets II.approach: Sort so duplicates are adjacent. Skip equal values at the SAME decision depth, but allow a second equal value in a deeper decision so [2,2] remains possible.
Subsets II.complexity: O(n*2^n) worst output/time plus sort; O(n) stack and copy before output.
Subsets II.trace: [1,2,2]: skip the second 2 as a root sibling, but permit it after taking the first 2.
Subsets II.pitfalls: Globally forbidding duplicates would incorrectly remove subsets that use repeated input positions.

Combination Sum III.problem: Select exactly k distinct digits from 1..9 whose sum is target.
Combination Sum III.approach: Choose increasing digits so each combination has one representation. State carries the next minimum digit, remaining count and remaining sum.
Combination Sum III.complexity: O(2^9*9) upper-bound enumeration time; O(9) working stack plus output.
Combination Sum III.trace: 1+2+6, 1+3+5 and 2+3+4 are the three valid triples for nine.
Combination Sum III.pitfalls: k=0,target=0 yields an empty combination. Digits cannot repeat.

Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.expected: [ad, ae, af, bd, be, bf, cd, ce, cf]
Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.problem: Return all letter strings represented by digits 2..9; empty input returns empty.
Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.approach: At each digit branch over its letters; copy the path after processing all digits. The product of independent per-digit choices gives every combination.
Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.trace: Choose a/b/c for 2, then d/e/f for 3.
Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.pitfalls: Digits 0/1 have no letters and are rejected rather than silently skipping positions.

Palindrome partitioning.problem: Partition the whole string into contiguous palindromic parts; return every partition.
Palindrome partitioning.approach: For each start, try every palindromic prefix and recursively partition the suffix. Each partition has a unique sequence of end positions.
Palindrome partitioning.complexity: O(n²*2^n) safe worst time bound for direct checks/copies; O(n) recursion depth plus output.
Palindrome partitioning.trace: a -> a -> b gives [a,a,b]; aa -> b gives [aa,b].
Palindrome partitioning.pitfalls: Empty string has one empty partition. Substring creates new strings in Java 8.
Palindrome partitioning.alternatives: Precompute a palindrome table in O(n²) to make each prefix check O(1); output remains exponential.

Word Search.problem: Find a word via orthogonal steps in a rectangular character board without reusing a cell.
Word Search.approach: Try each start and recursively match one character per step. Mark a cell only for the current path, restoring it before returning so other paths may use it.
Word Search.complexity: O(rows*cols*4^wordLength) safe upper bound; O(rows*cols+wordLength) auxiliary space.
Word Search.pitfalls: A global permanently visited set is wrong: reuse is forbidden within a path, not across alternative searches.

N Queen.problem: Return all n-by-n boards with n nonattacking queens, one in each row.
N Queen.approach: Place one queen per row. Boolean column and two diagonal arrays give O(1) conflict tests. Mark -> recurse -> unmark explores every valid placement.
N Queen.complexity: O(n*n!) search upper bound plus O(n²) copying per result; O(n²) board and O(n) stack/flags.
N Queen.trace: For n=4, columns [1,3,0,2] and [2,0,3,1] are the two valid boards.
N Queen.pitfalls: Diagonal indices are r-c+n-1 and r+c. n=0 gives one empty board.

Rat in a Maze.problem: Return all simple open-cell paths in a square binary maze, top-left to bottom-right; directions D,L,R,U.
Rat in a Maze.approach: DFS marks only the current path. Explore directions in lexical order and restore visits so distinct paths remain possible.
Rat in a Maze.complexity: Exponential path enumeration, O(4^(n²)) loose upper bound; O(n²) working space plus output.
Rat in a Maze.trace: For [[1,0],[1,1]], only down then right reaches the destination.
Rat in a Maze.pitfalls: A blocked endpoint yields empty. A 1x1 open maze has one empty path, whose list prints ambiguously as [].

M Coloring Problem.problem: Decide whether an undirected adjacency-matrix graph can be properly colored with at most m colors.
M Coloring Problem.approach: Choose a color for the next vertex only if no neighbor already has it. Recursively complete later vertices; restore failed choices. Every possible valid assignment is explored.
M Coloring Problem.complexity: O(V*m^V) loose time upper bound; O(V) colors/stack excluding input.
M Coloring Problem.trace: A triangle needs three different colors; two cannot suffice.
M Coloring Problem.pitfalls: A self-loop makes proper coloring impossible. Empty graph is colorable with zero colors.

Sudoku Solver.problem: Solve a 9x9 Sudoku in place, with . for blanks. Return false if invalid or unsolvable, restoring attempted blank assignments.
Sudoku Solver.approach: Validate initial clues, then fill the first blank with each row/column/box-compatible digit. A failed continuation restores the blank. An all-filled valid board is the base success.
Sudoku Solver.complexity: O(9^E) loose upper bound for E blanks with constant-size checks; O(E) stack.
Sudoku Solver.trace: First-row blanks are constrained by column and 3x3 box; the completed first row is 534678912.
Sudoku Solver.pitfalls: Initial duplicates must be detected, otherwise an already-full invalid board would wrongly return true.

Expression Add Operators.problem: Insert +,-,* between digit groups to reach target; preserve digit order, use no parentheses and forbid multi-digit leading-zero operands.
Expression Add Operators.approach: Track total and the last signed multiplicative term. Multiplication replaces last with last*x in total, enforcing precedence without reparsing. Try all token endpoints and all operators.
Expression Add Operators.complexity: Exponential O(n*4^n) loose search/string-cost bound, with additional BigInteger bit costs; O(n) depth plus expression storage/output.
Expression Add Operators.trace: 1+2 then *3 would replace +2 with +6, giving 7; 1*2*3 correctly evaluates 6.
Expression Add Operators.pitfalls: BigInteger prevents expression overflow. A token 0 is valid, but 00 is not.

Sort a Stack Using Recursion.problem: Sort stack descending from top to bottom, using front as top.
Sort a Stack Using Recursion.approach: Recursively sort the remaining stack; insert the removed top by recursively moving larger entries aside until its proper position, then restore them.
Sort a Stack Using Recursion.complexity: O(n²) time, O(n) peak recursion depth.
Sort a Stack Using Recursion.trace: Sort1,3,2 into3,2,1; insert4 at the top.
Sort a Stack Using Recursion.pitfalls: Equal values are allowed. Iterative collection sorting is simpler when recursion is not an exercise requirement.

Subset Sums Enumeration.problem: Return sums of all POSITIONAL subsets sorted, including duplicate sums and empty sum zero.
Subset Sums Enumeration.approach: Take/skip each index; each leaf is exactly one positional subset and contributes its accumulated sum.
Subset Sums Enumeration.complexity: O(2^n log(2^n)) sorting time, O(2^n) output and O(n) stack.
Subset Sums Enumeration.trace: Skip both0; only1 gives1; only2 gives2; both gives3.
Subset Sums Enumeration.pitfalls: Unlike distinct-subset enumeration, repeated sum values must not be removed. Exponential output limits practical n.

Recursive String to Integer.problem: Recursive atoi: skip ASCII spaces, optional sign, read decimal prefix and clamp to signed int.
Recursive String to Integer.approach: Recursion consumes one digit per frame. Check the limit before multiplying, and immediately return the clamped limit if it would be exceeded.
Recursive String to Integer.complexity: O(n) time/stack, stopping early after saturation.
Recursive String to Integer.trace: 2147483649 exceeds negative magnitude limit2147483648, so result clamps to MIN_VALUE.
Recursive String to Integer.pitfalls: Very long strings of leading zeros still recurse deeply without saturation; the iterative atoi lesson is preferable for production input.
